title: Knee sprain at a walking event
setting: Large charity walk. 23F slipped descending a steep slope. Sitting on the ground, complaining of severe knee pain, won't bear weight.
verdictExplanation: Alert, airway clear, breathing and circulation normal. An isolated, painful soft-tissue knee injury with no red flags. Injured but not sick: treat on scene.

history.history: Injury occurred moments ago, slipped descending a muddy path
history.injuries: Knee swelling and bruising, tender to touch
history.additional: Carries adrenaline injector for shellfish allergy but no allergy signs

followUp.question: Which of the following would be a red flag indicating this is more than a simple sprain?

options.text: Inability to bear weight after resting, or visible deformity
A pain score of 7/10 immediately after the fall
Slight swelling and bruising developing over time
The patient feeling tearful and anxious

followUp.explanation: While pain, swelling, and anxiety are expected with a sprain, inability to bear weight (Ottawa ankle/knee rules) or visible deformity are red flags that warrant onward assessment for a fracture or severe ligamentous injury.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Support and advise rest. Warn that if pain worsens or she cannot weight-bear after rest, she should seek onward medical assessment.
levelFlags.erNotes: Assess distal circulation and sensation. Offer appropriate analgesia within scope and reassess pain after treatment.
